The geometry proof compares dimensions rather than asserting a skeleton exists, which is the distinction that makes it a test of this clause at all: the PRIMARY parses the built stylesheet with an exact standalone-selector matcher -- so a density variant such as `:root[data-hcm-density="compact"] .work-row` cannot be mistaken for the base rule -- and requires each proxy and its resolved counterpart to declare identical `min-height`. It was verified against the pre-fix values and failed there. REFACTOR's single model is `AsyncRegionState` with exactly the five states named -- Loading, Empty, Stale, Failure, Resolved -- as an int enum whose **zero value is Loading, not Resolved**. That direction is the load-bearing one here: a region descriptor that forgets to set its state renders through the sized skeleton rather than as a false-resolved empty box, which is precisely the shift. `UsesGeometryProxy` and `Announcement` switch over all five members with no default branch, returning `ErrUnknownAsyncRegionState` for anything outside the set. The fault clause is proven stronger than size compatibility: `BuildFailure` renders through the same `loadingProxyBody` call as the loading builders, and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Fault` requires the loading and failure bodies to be **byte-identical** for People, Work and Organization, so a region cannot collapse when its fetch fails. The Performance entry asserts a deterministic shift score (`|delta height| / viewport height`) rather than elapsed wall-clock time, deliberately avoiding this machine's unreliable timing, and separately proves the check rejects a real violation. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. Cumulative layout shift measured through a `PerformanceObserver` on `layout-shift` entries with `buffered: true`, excluding entries with recent input: `/workspace/app/people` resolved **20 rendered rows with CLS 0.00000 and zero shift entries** -- a real skeleton-to-content transition rather than a trivially empty page -- and `/workspace/app/work` likewise measured zero. Software navigation was tested by clicking a real navigation link from People to Organization: the `.app-shell` and `nav.primary-nav` elements are the **same DOM nodes** before and after, disproving RED's remount clause directly, with CLS 0.00000 across the transition. **Boundaries.** No governed numeric CLS budget exists anywhere in the repository -- `page_performance_budgets.go` is an honest stub that refuses to invent one until a governed service publishes -- so `AsyncRegionLayoutShiftBudget = 0.1` is declared as an engineering threshold, documented as not business-authoritative, in the same category as `latencygate`'s hardcoded p95 figures. The Organization and Insights loading families were not individually re-verified pixel-for-pixel; only the People, Work and History row families were fixed and proven. `BuildFailure` and `BuildAsyncRegion` are tested primitives not yet wired into the live wasm router's fetch-error path. History's resolved row has no declared `min-height`, being content-driven, so its parity with the shared proxy could not be proven pixel-exact the way People's could. The pre-existing `appShellWithHeading` LoadError branch was deliberately left alone as a different working contract.
  - **Progress (2026-09-13):** The Go/WASM route loader now passes a subject-sanitized warm baseline into the product client; changing Person, Work, History, Organization or Journey identity clears route-owned selection before a new server projection arrives. Focused UXAUDIT-012 tests pass, and a live global-search switch from Sofia to Rosa resolved only Rosa's profile. An actual delayed-network visual/CLS/focus/scroll matrix across every page is still required; this todo remains open.

The orchestrator chose this over opening `WorkService` to the browser, which would have widened `journeyclient/rpc_adapter.go`'s deliberate JourneyService-only allowlist. `internal/intent/app/journey_work_summary.go` builds it from the work items the list already loads (no added reads) and discloses nothing unless `workitem.Visible` admits the viewer; the assignee additionally requires `workitem.ContextVisible`, actions are exactly `workitem.PermittedActions`, and display names resolve only by exact worker id or key, memoized and capped at 16 principals per page. The real-database Security test proves an ASSIGNEE_ONLY approval discloses no summary to its author or an outsider. **My Work** is an action queue ordered by urgency tier (repair, then blocked or awaiting approval, then waiting, then terminal), then the viewer's standing on the current work item (holds, may claim, others), then stage-derived person-versus-workflow ownership, then the real due date; rows lead with `Your next action` drawn only from server-granted actions, then the next step, assignment and due date, falling back to the stage-derived next step and waiting-on line plus one honest note when no summary is disclosed. An `Assigned to me` tab (`filter=mine`) scopes to work the viewer holds or may claim; the default view stays all authorized journeys because scoping it would hide a proposer's PROPOSED and BLOCKED journeys, which have no work item. Filter links always carry an explicit `filter=`, fixing a defect where a saved My Work filter could never be cleared. **Journeys** is a lifecycle tracker grouped by subject with each group's statuses and a next step per open card, both pages deep-link to `/workspace/app/journeys?journey=<id>`, and the two empty states differ. **Live verification** on the rebuilt cell (wasm bundle hash matched its manifest): as `hc-054-thomas-baker`, the routed ASSIGNEE_ONLY finance approver, Dominic's and Aya's rows read `Your next action: Claim`, `Assigned to you`, `Due 2026-09-15` and `filter=mine` narrowed seven journeys to those two; as `principal:promotion-approver` and as the admin persona the same rows showed only the stage fallback and note, as the visibility rule requires. **The 390px pass found a defect every HTML-string test missed:** a pre-existing `.work-row .row-main small+small { display:none }` below 1190px hid every row line after the first `<small>`, so on phones, tablets and narrow laptops the queue showed none of the next action, next step, assignment or due date -- and had been silently hiding PROMOUX-003's disposition line too. The orchestrator scoped the rule to a new `row-summary` class so only the grade-change line drops, re-verified at 390px that all facts render with no horizontal scroll, and added `TestWorkRowActionFactsSurviveNarrowWidths`, which fails naming the selector when the positional rule is restored. Mutations verified by name: dropping the ownership or due-date sort keys, `Assigned to me` returning all work, offering a next action without a matching grant (initially survived; the test was tightened), disclosing an assignee without `ContextVisible`, `governed=true`, skipping `Visible`, dropping the wire copy or client projection, removing the name-lookup cap, and restoring the `small+small` rule. Recorded, not fixed: `ListJourneys` already performed one record read per journey and re-simulated unexecuted journeys before this change, so the page is not yet truly batched; the two status vocabularies still differ (`Proposed` versus `Ready to start approval`, and RECORDED is open on Journeys but closed on My Work); the `Awaiting approval` tab matches only its own label, so Manager and Finance approval journeys never appear in it; and in the dev personas the only routed finance approver, Thomas Baker, is the self-service Finance Director persona, which reaches only Myself, Organization and Insights, so signed in through the persona picker he cannot open My Work to act on his own approvals.
  - **Progress (2026-09-13):** My Work now explicitly scopes its subtitle and Review/Blocked empty states to the signed-in person's assignments, with localized due labels; Journeys retains the separate live promotion lifecycle groups. Focused UXAUDIT-017 tests, productui vet and the full productui package suite pass. In the rebuilt Codex browser, Rafael's zero-item Review and Blocked filters explained their assigned scope, and the Track promotion requests link opened Journeys while browser Back preserved the Blocked filter. A live assigned nonempty queue, urgency ordering and return-to-canonical-intent behavior still need multi-persona browser/integration evidence; the todo remains open.

Search is fuzzy, ranked and multi-typed live: `adrian` returns four options typed Person, Workflow, Action and Setting, the misspelled `insigths` still resolves Insights as a Page, `org` returns eight including Organization and Organization visibility, and `zzzznope` returns the empty state. Favorites stay discoverable as a `.nav-favorite` control on every `.nav-entry`. Earlier work had therefore already fixed the behavior and never written the tests this todo names, so the whole risk here was authoring a suite against behavior that already passes, which passes on its first run by construction and proves nothing. Every one of the six tests was consequently mutation-verified against a real break in production code: dropping the `Keywords` half of `navigationItemFromDefinition` failed the PRIMARY with `NavItem.Keywords = []`; swapping `html.Details`/`html.Summary` for `html.Div` failed the ACCESSIBILITY with `group must be a native <details>/<summary> disclosure`; weakening `authorizedGlobalSearchItems` from `if ok && allowed[definition.ID]` to `if ok` failed the SECURITY on its zero-grant bundle with `search item "page:help" ... resolves to page "help", which roleaccess denies this role bundle View on`; removing the early exit in `globalSearchScore` moved P95 from roughly 10ms to roughly 30ms past the 20ms budget and failed the PERFORMANCE; making `navigationSearchScore` ignore `item.Keywords` failed the REGRESSION with `alias "dashboard" resolves in menu filtering=false but in global search=true`, and making `BrandLogo` default to a fabricated `harborcare-logo.svg` failed its second pin; dropping `ID: "global-search-input"` from `GlobalSearch` failed the BROWSER naming that exact fragment. The SECURITY test is a property over sixteen role bundles resolved through `roleaccess.DefaultPagePermissions`, `EffectivePagePermissions` and `CanPageAction` rather than through `productui.PageVisible`, because `product_shell.go` overrides the registry fallback with `roleaccess.CanPageAction` whenever page permissions are configured and `roleaccessstore.Store.Bootstrap` always configures them, so the registry is not the authority a live server enforces. It is pinned live: signed in as the `worker_self` persona, searching `adrian` -- a worker outside that viewer's authority -- and `roles` -- the Admin roles page -- both return the empty state, while `organ` returns three authorized results, proving the empty answers are scoping rather than a broken search, and the same persona receives 403 on `/people`, `/journeys`, `/work`, `/history`, `/admin` and `/admin/roles` against 200 on `/insights`, `/myself` and `/organization`. Two deliberate non-defects were examined rather than "fixed": the brand slot renders `data-hcm-brand-logo-state="fallback"` with a `src`-less `<img>` because `BrandLogoURL` is an administrator-supplied preference that is empty by default, and that image computes `display:none` at 0x0 so no broken-image icon or layout cost results while a `.sr-only` span still names the home link -- the REGRESSION test now forbids fabricating a default asset; and a `worker_self` searching their own name returns nothing because Person-kind results are gated on the People grant as a whole, which is consistent with being unable to browse any coworker, `myself` remaining reachable by its own search terms. One real latent weakness was found and left deliberately in place with coverage: `globalSearchItems` injects Help and Settings candidates unconditionally and relies entirely on `authorizedGlobalSearchItems` to strip them, a reliance invisible to any named-role test because every real role happens to hold `help`, so the zero-grant bundle stays first in the SECURITY matrix permanently. **Boundary.** The CSS cascade facts above -- computed `white-space`, `overflow-y`, `scrollbar-width` and real `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` -- cannot be proven from a Go unit test; they are asserted only in the unexecuted Playwright spec, and the live run recorded here is what actually proves them.

## 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation

These items are the atomic follow-up to the 2026-09-12 live promotion review. The observed journey `01a09550-c0b6-70d2-9aaf-2f90701ca0c4` advanced durably through proposal, simulation, admission, finance approval and manager approval to `wait_effective_date`; the contracts below address the integrity and usability defects encountered on that path. `UXAUDIT-002` remains the end-to-end closure gate.

- [x] `PROMOUX-001` **[P0][SOL_HIGH] Resolve promotion eligibility consistently across the seeded workforce.**
  - **Depends:** `PROMO-007`, `JOBARCH-004`, `WEB-109`, `WEB-119`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=EXPOSURE; SETS=BI.PEOPLE,BI.REWARDS; INTENTS=PromoteWorker; DIRECT=none; WHY=make eligible promotion subjects discoverable from one coherent authorized workforce projection`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Integration`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Browser`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security`; `REGRESSION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression`.
  - **RED:** Journeys sends users to a directory where every initially visible worker reports `No available workflows`, the sole eligible Jane record can be found only by knowing her name, or the legacy `W-1001` corpus record and the 64 seeded workers follow different promotion-eligibility rules.
  - **GREEN:** the authorized directory can filter directly to promotion-eligible workers, every displayed availability state has a server-provided reason, local-dev fixtures use one worker identity and job-architecture model, and at least four role-diverse workers exercise eligible, ineligible, active-conflict and withheld outcomes without enumeration leakage.
  - **REFACTOR:** eligibility is one server-owned projection consumed by People, Person, global actions and Journeys; no client-side role-code allowlist.
  - **Refs:** [promotion workflow](reference-workflows/promote-into-management.md), `internal/intent/app`, `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`, `test/workspace`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux001_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_WorkerCreationReservationIsAtomicWithItsWorker` in `internal/intent/app` (`promoux001_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Browser` in `tools/uxqual/browser/promoux001_people_eligibility.spec.mjs`; new `internal/humanwork/productui/promotion_availability.go` and `internal/data/demoworkforce/promotion_paths.go`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 93.4% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 84.8% (`tools/uxqual/productclient`), 53.5% (`internal/data/demoworkforce`), 43.2% (`internal/intent/app`) and 68.0% (`internal/data/workeridstore`) -- the last three sit under recorded `below_floor` exceptions that this change raised rather than created; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires.** The dev stack was rebuilt (schema 285, `demo-people` seeded), and the People directory at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/workspace/app/people` was driven in a real browser: 65 people across Finance, Marketing, Legal & Compliance and Care Coordination, a `Promotion-eligible only` checkbox in the filter form, 30 of 50 visible rows offering a Workflows menu, and the remaining 20 carrying the server-provided reason `No eligible promotion role is published for this employee. Ask your HR administrator to review the job ladder and pay band.` The bare `No available workflows` string that RED names is gone from the live surface. `?eligible=1` narrows the directory to 38 rows, every one of them offering a workflow and none carrying an unavailable reason. The root cause RED describes was a job-architecture catalog gap rather than a business-rule refusal: `workforceOptions()` published promotion paths only from the fixed four-worker corpus, whose job codes do not overlap the 60 demoworkforce codes, so every seeded worker resolved zero choices for a structural reason indistinguishable from ineligibility. `demoworkforce.PromotionPaths()` now publishes the demo company's own computed ladder into the same `WorkforceOptions` contract. Enumeration leakage is closed in both directions. `ResolvePromotionAvailability(authorized, hasPath, activeConflict)` checks authorization first and exhaustively, with no permissive default, so every worker collapses to one `PromotionWithheld` code for an unauthorized viewer; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security` drives three different underlying states through an unauthorized viewer and requires exactly one distinct reason string, then requires ineligible and active-conflict to differ for an authorized one. A zero-value trap was closed during review: `personPromotionEligible` treated an unset `PromotionAvailability` as eligible, and the regression test asserted that an unevaluated worker received a launchable action and no reason at all -- a Person built by any future page, provider or partial projection would have offered a promotion the server never authorized. The gate now requires an explicit `PromotionEligible`, the shared fixtures say so, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression` pins both halves; restoring the permissive gate fails it with `a worker with no server verdict was offered a launchable promotion`. Two independent defects were fixed alongside. `demo-people` could not seed at all because `ingestDemoPhotos` demanded bit-identical regeneration of proxies whose checked-in bytes had drifted for `hc-042`/`hc-055`; it now trusts an already-published tracked proxy, and no tracked asset bytes were modified. And `workeridstore.Store.Reserve` self-committed while `journeyEngine.CreateWorker` inserted the worker row in a separate later transaction, so any failure between the two permanently orphaned a worker number in an append-only reservation table; `ReserveTx` now threads the caller's transaction through both steps. **Boundaries.** The Playwright spec was written but not executed here; the live evidence above is a real browser driven against the real server, not that spec. `TestTodo_SVC_013_Integration` in `cmd/migrate` fails on migration rollback, which is pre-existing -- 00284 raises the same irreversible exception and predates this work.

- [x] `PROMOUX-002` **[P0][SOL_HIGH] Prevent overlapping active promotions and route users to the existing journey.**
  - **Depends:** `PROMO-007`, `WF-RUN-018`, `WEB-119`, `WEB-132`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.PEOPLE,BI.REWARDS; INTENTS=PromoteWorker; DIRECT=none; WHY=prevent conflicting promotion intent while preserving continuity to the active request`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Integration`; `RACE=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Browser`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security`; `RECOVERY=TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Recovery`.
  - **RED:** a worker with a nonterminal promotion still exposes `Start Promotion`, or concurrent starts create more than one active promotion before execution-time conflict checking.
  - **GREEN:** a tenant-scoped active-intent guard admits exactly one promotion per worker and overlapping effective window; replays resolve to the same intent; People and Person replace Start with `Open active promotion`; a conflicting actor sees a safe explanation and zero new proposal, work item or domain mutation.
  - **REFACTOR:** the guard belongs to promotion admission and is projected to clients; UI suppression is not the integrity boundary.
  - **Refs:** [promotion workflow](reference-workflows/promote-into-management.md), `internal/domains/promotion`, `internal/data/intentcontrol`, `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-12):** `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Recovery` in `internal/data/promotionguard` (`guard_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race` in `internal/data/promotionguard` (`race_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` in `test/bootstrap` (`promoux002_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux002_test.go`); new `migrations/00286_promoux002_active_promotion_guard.sql`, `internal/data/promotionguard` and `internal/intent/app/promotionguard_wire.go`. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.6% (`internal/data/promotionguard`), 81.1% (`internal/transport/journey`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 81.7% (`internal/data/schema`), 81.5% (`migrations`) and 53.8% (`cmd/migrate`), with `internal/humanwork/workspace` and `internal/intent/app` raised under their recorded `below_floor` exceptions rather than newly violating them; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. REFACTOR's clause -- the guard belongs to promotion admission and UI suppression is not the integrity boundary -- is what this todo turns on, so the guarantee is a database constraint rather than an application check. `promotion_active_intent_guard` carries a partial unique index on `(tenant_id, worker_ref, effective_date) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'`, and `promotionguard.Admit` is a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` -- never a SELECT that precedes the write. Two concurrent transactions may both read no conflict; only one can commit, because PostgreSQL evaluates the index as part of each INSERT's own commit. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race` proves it with 12 goroutines on genuinely independent connections and transactions released from a common barrier, each presenting a distinct idempotency key so the test measures exclusion between different requests rather than deduplication of one retry, and asserts exactly one admission plus a durable row count rather than merely the absence of an error. The zero-mutation clause is proven by counting rather than by asserting success, twice over: a `countingExecutor`/`countingBeginner` wrapping the real `dbport.Tx` (the pattern `internal/humanwork/workitem/decide_approval_test.go` established) requires every mutating statement a refused start issues to target `promotion_active_intent_guard` and nothing else, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` additionally diffs row counts across `intent_instance`, `ledger_event`, `work_item` and the domain tables. The guard is proven to hold with the UI entirely out of the picture: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` calls `journeyEngine.Propose` directly with no HTTP, gRPC or page involved, and the PRIMARY calls `Admit` directly. Four pre-existing tests were updated rather than weakened, each of which had assumed two proposals for one worker's single effective date are both admitted -- the exact defect this todo closes. `TestTodo_PROMO_007_Integration`'s digest subtest now asserts the second request is refused with `journey.propose_promotion.active_conflict`, keeps its original content-digest claim by computing `app.PromotionProposeRequestDigest` on the refused request directly, and adds a row count proving no second intent was created; `TestTodo_PROMO_007_Mutation`, `TestTodo_WF_RUN_027_Bootstrap_Security` and `TestJourneyDecideRejectReachesTheRejectedTerminal` now use distinct, non-overlapping effective dates so their own zero-effect and terminal claims still exercise two genuinely admitted proposals. **Boundary, and it is a real one.** `promotionguard.Release` is implemented and unit-tested but is called from no production code, because no write-time hook fires when an intent reaches a terminal stage (`deriveJourneyStage` is read-time only, computed from workflow runtime nodes). A guard row is therefore created ACTIVE and never closed, so once a promotion is rejected or completed, re-proposing for that same worker and effective date is refused permanently; the workaround is a different effective date. This also disagrees with the UI, whose `activeConflict` signal still comes from the pre-existing `ListJourneys` non-terminal scan rather than the guard table, so after a journey goes terminal the UI offers Start while the server refuses it. RED frames the guard around a worker with a _nonterminal_ promotion, so blocking past terminal is outside the contract this todo was built for; escalated separately rather than left implied. Two registry rows were added during review that the lane could not write itself: `promotion_active_intent_guard`, and `ledger_payload_disposition`, which LEDGER-011 shipped without a `definitions/storage/storage-disposition.yaml` entry and which had left `TestTodo_DATA_001` red since that merge.

Cycle safety is real reachability rather than a single-hop guard. `org.DetectManagerCycle` walks the proposed manager's actual ancestor chain through `ResolveManagerRelationships` and asks whether the promoted worker appears in it, so a cycle that closes two or more hops up is caught; `TestDetectManagerCycle_MultiHop` and the PRIMARY's multi-hop subtest both build A reports to B reports to C and refuse promoting A to manage C, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Integration` reproduces that same shape against real PostgreSQL rows. The review card shows the manager as a raw worker id because no directory lookup is reachable from `productui`, the boundary PROMOUX-003 recorded. The full `test/bootstrap` and root suites were not run, per AGENTS.md's multi-hour guidance; every golden that actually broke was regenerated through its own package's `-update` flag.

No pre-existing test file was edited. The clause that carries this todo is that an authority-filtered invalidation carries a sequence, and those two requirements interact as a disclosure bug rather than a cosmetic one: with a global sequence and a filter that merely drops undeliverable messages, a viewer who observes 1, 2, 4 has learned that event 3 exists and can count promotions they hold no authority over. The scheme chosen is gap-free renumbering per subscriber. `promotioninvalidation.NextSequence` allocates each committed transition a durable global position through `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`, evaluated inside each writer's own commit so concurrent writers cannot lose or duplicate one, but that value never reaches the wire -- it serves only as an item's revision for stale and reorder protection. `SubscriberSequencer.EmitForSubscriber` mints each subscriber its own counter and advances it by exactly one **only when a message is actually delivered**, so a transition authorising nothing for that subscriber never touches their counter and their visible sequence is contiguous by construction. The proof reproduces the leak before fixing it, which is what distinguishes it from a test that merely asserts the corrected behaviour: the PRIMARY's `subscriber_sequencer_closes_the_disclosure_gap_the_naive_scheme_leaks` subtest first runs the naive scheme and observes the delivered pair `[1, 3]` with a gap of 2, then runs the real one and requires `[1, 2]` with a delta of exactly 1. Region isolation is proven against real `tools/uxqual/invalidation.Client` instances rather than a stub: a Detail-region message for one worker fires exactly the matching client once and leaves a My-Work client and a different worker's Detail client at zero, so REFACTOR's prohibition on a full-shell reload is enforced rather than assumed. Last-updated is proven equal to the newest transition's own `OccurredAt` regardless of input order, with an empty set rendering an empty string rather than falling back to the current time. The no-duplicate-render clause is counted rather than inferred, because a double render converges to the same state and would pass any state assertion: the Recovery test counts `Refetch` invocations across a reconnect that redelivers an already-applied sequence before a genuinely new one, and requires exactly two. The Performance entry asserts delivered-message counts and bounded per-subscriber state rather than elapsed time, deliberately avoiding this machine's unreliable wall-clock behaviour. Zero values fail closed throughout: `RegionCursor{}` refuses any incoming value including 0, `Transition{}` and zero-revision or zero-timestamp variants fail `Validate()`, and the sequencer never advances on an undelivered message. **A defect I introduced was found by this lane and corrected here.** The `ledger_payload_disposition` row I added during PROMOUX-002 review declared `data_role: EVIDENCE` and `retention_class: EVIDENCE`, neither of which is a declared value -- `data_role` admits only LEDGER, PROJECTION, OUTBOX, REGISTRY, CONTROL and AGGREGATE, and `retention_class` only PERMANENT, OPERATIONAL and REBUILDABLE. It broke `TestTodo_STORE_001` and `TestTodo_STORE_001_Mutation` and had escaped notice because that gate lives in `internal/data/tenancy/storagedisposition`, a different package from the `TestTodo_DATA_001` check run at the time. Corrected to LEDGER and PERMANENT, matching `ledger_event` itself. **Boundaries.** The components are not wired into a live promotion page, the same boundary PROMOUX-003, 005, 006 and 007 recorded and which is escalated for all of them together; no production caller yet invokes `NextSequence` from a committed-transition write path, which lies outside this todo's Refs. DOM scroll and focus preservation on reconnect is asserted structurally -- region containers are independently addressable -- because it cannot be proven in a non-browser Go test, and the Recovery test says so in its own comment.

Three RPCs were added to `JourneyService` -- `EditProposal`, `PreviewJourneyIntervention` (read-only) and `RequestJourneyIntervention` -- each carrying the file's own `Effect class:` disposition comment verified through a descriptor-based totality test, plus a shared `hcmnext.common.v1.InterventionOutcome` enum (`APPLIED|PENDING_SAFE_POINT|DENIED|TOO_LATE|REPAIR_REQUIRED`) and `Journey.governance_version`, the intent's own optimistic-concurrency version, which nothing on this wire exposed before. `buf generate` is byte-identical across two runs and touches only the three expected files, independently reproduced at review time by regenerating and comparing digests. The wire change was necessary because `DecideJourneyRequest` carried only `{intent_id, approve bool, reason}` -- an approve/reject binary with no room for withdraw, cancel, supersede or edit. **The implementation reused the existing domain capability rather than reimplementing it, and discovering that `SupersedeIntent` could not be reused at all was the key finding.** `promote_worker` is P1A/`simulateOnlyChangeTransitions`, whose `SUPERSEDED` edges exist only from `SIMULATED`, `SUBMITTED` or `APPROVED`; a journey's stored intent never durably leaves `DRAFT`, and the kernel's own lifecycle profile has no `DRAFT` to `SUPERSEDED` edge, so `SupersedeIntent` is structurally unusable here. `EditProposal` therefore composes `CancelIntent` -- legal from `DRAFT` and already safe-point-aware for a mid-flight `EXECUTING` journey -- followed by an ordinary `Propose` once the cancellation disposition is genuinely `CANCELLED`, which makes GREEN's requirement that edits create a new proposal revision and invalidate material approvals literally true: the original carries the approval, the original is what is durably cancelled, and the successor inherits nothing. **Three real defects were found by running the code rather than reasoning about it, each observed failing before the fix and passing after.** `lifecycle_endpoints.go`'s `SupersedeIntent` minted and durably appended the successor intent before validating and applying the original's own transition, so a refused or raced supersede left an orphaned successor behind -- a genuine partial write, now reordered so the original's compare-and-swap lands first. `journey_decide.go`'s `Decide` and `Execute` checked no terminal `RequestState`, so a journey cancelled mid-flight could still be decided or executed; both now carry a terminal-state guard. And `internal/data/promotionguard.Release` was dead code by its own doc comment, so a cancelled-then-reproposed journey for the same worker and effective date would have refused itself as a duplicate; it is now called on a successful `CANCELLED` disposition. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Race` drives 8 concurrent goroutines -- 4 `EditProposal`, 4 `RequestJourneyIntervention(WITHDRAW)` -- through the production connection pool against one real proposed journey, all presenting the same expected version, and asserts durable state rather than return codes: exactly one successor intent exists if an edit won and zero if a withdraw won, which is what would have caught the orphaned-successor defect directly. The UI is wired end to end rather than left as an unreachable capability: `reviewSurface` needed no changes because PROMOUX-010's prop contract was deliberately built to accommodate Withdraw and Cancel, so this was plumbing through `journeyclient`, and Withdraw, Cancel and Edit render at every stage -- disabled with a named reason when unavailable rather than omitted, since an omitted action is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. `interventionNotice` reports the typed outcome truthfully instead of always claiming cancellation. The disclosure rule is proven by value in the I18N test, which asserts the disabled-reason text is byte-identical across two journeys sharing a terminal stage but differing in worker name and correlation id -- the same pattern PROMOUX-001 and PROMOUX-004 established. **A client-side mirror of the server's stage-availability rule was accepted but required a test, and the lane was sent back for it.** `journeyclient.InterventionAvailability` mirrors `internal/intent/app`'s unexported `interventionUnavailableAtStage` so availability cannot go stale between watch pushes; it is a presentation hint rather than an authorization decision, since the server refuses on submit regardless, but an untested mirror drifts silently and the failure mode is a user confidently told an action is unavailable when it is not. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_ClientServerAvailabilityAgreement` now runs both implementations across the full cross product of 15 stages by 2 kinds, reading the stage and kind lists from the generated enums' own `_name` maps rather than a hardcoded list so a newly added stage fails the test instead of being silently skipped, with a hard failure if either map is empty or names a kind the test does not cover; all 30 pairs agree on both availability and reason reference. Mutation-verified by dropping `stageBlocked` from the client's unstarted check, which failed exactly two pairs by name -- `WITHDRAW at BLOCKED` and `CANCEL at BLOCKED` -- while the other 28 kept passing. The three UI tests were each mutation-verified too: dropping `DisabledReason` failed the BROWSER naming `disabled action "withdraw" has no reason paragraph`; renaming the reason field's label and dropping `Required` failed the ACCESSIBILITY naming `no visible label "Reason" found`; and forcing the static description in place of the server preview failed the I18N naming that the server-worded consequence summary did not survive rendering byte-for-byte. **Boundaries, recorded rather than glossed.** The I18N test proves the plumbing survives translated and bidi content but does not prove localized delivery, because `tools/uxqual/render/journey` has no locale catalog and emits no `dir="rtl"` anywhere -- every string including PROMOUX-010's is fixed English Go source, and building that catalog is a separate and much larger effort. Consequence previews refresh on detail load and after an intervention rather than on every watch tick, so the server's worded consequence sentence has a bounded staleness window; availability and reason text never go stale, being computed from the always-fresh stage. Edit's job-code and base-pay fields pre-fill from display strings rather than parsed values, which is cosmetic because the reviewer retypes them. `EP-WF-002` was deliberately not implemented, but `InterventionOutcome` and `workspace.JourneyInterventionOutcome` are placed in shared locations specifically so its Pause, Resume, Cancel and RetryNode work can adopt the same five-value vocabulary rather than inventing a second one. **One infrastructure landmine was found and independently reproduced:** `buf.gen.yaml` declares `clean: true` over the whole `gen/go` tree, which also holds `gen/go/hcmnext/model/model_generated.go`, a non-buf output from `tools/gen/modelgen`, so every `buf generate` silently deletes it -- verified at review time by running `buf generate` and watching the file disappear, then restoring it byte-identical with `go run ./tools/gen/modelgen/cmd/modelgen`. That is the true cause of a phantom missing-`gen/go/hcmnext/model` build failure another lane hit earlier the same day, which was initially misattributed to a concurrency race. It needs a permanent fix -- a combined regeneration script or a separate output root -- and is filed separately rather than patched here.

Admission and intent creation are still two transactions, so crash/orphan reconciliation remains the open gate.

## 71. Live visual-design and interaction polish

These items qualify the rendered production frontend against the design-token contracts already completed under `WEB-013` through `WEB-024`. They are not a redesign fork: each item removes observed inconsistency from the shared Go components and must be verified on the real server-backed pages.

- [x] `UIPOLISH-004` **[P0][SOL_HIGH] Give each page and component an explicit scroll owner.**
  - **Depends:** `WEB-023`, `WEB-037`, `WEB-047`, `UXAUDIT-008`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=EXPOSURE; SETS=BI.EXPERIENCE; DIRECT=none; WHY=preserve navigation, context and focus while large server-backed regions scroll`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004`; `BROWSER=TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Browser`; `ACCESSIBILITY=TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Accessibility`; `PERFORMANCE=TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Performance`; `REGRESSION=TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Regression`.
  - **RED:** navigation scrolls with page content, page and table compete for the same gesture, horizontal overflow is hidden, sticky headers detach from columns, popovers create accidental body scroll, or a styled scrollbar intrudes into content.
  - **GREEN:** the shell, navigation, page, table, drawer and overlay declare noncompeting scroll ownership; sticky headers and action bars remain within their container; focus is never hidden; keyboard, wheel, touch and RTL horizontal scrolling work; scrollbar size, contrast, gutter and edge placement use theme tokens and meet target requirements.
  - **REFACTOR:** one scroll-region component owns overflow, shadows, restoration, reduced motion and accessible naming.
  - **Refs:** [frontend plan](specs/production-frontend-and-page-composition.md), `tools/uxqual/render/journey`, `tools/uxqual/productclient`.
  - **Evidence (2026-09-13):** `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Browser`, `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Performance` and `TestTodo_UIPOLISH_004_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`todo_uipolish_004_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.4%; `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` and gofmt clean on every touched file; branch main. **RED reproduced live before the change** at 1440x900 on `/workspace/app/people`: three scroll regions were configured ad hoc and disagreed with each other. `.main-scroll` computed `scrollbar-width: auto` with `scrollbar-color: auto` -- a 15px native bar -- against `.primary-nav` and `.data-table-scroll` both using `thin` plus a themed token, and it carried no `role`, no `tabindex` and no accessible name at all while scrolling 466px, so a keyboard user could not reach it. `.action-launcher-dialog` was a fourth untokenized region. **Verified live after the change**, rebuilding the wasm bundle then the server binary in that order: all five regions now render through one `ScrollRegion` component and agree -- `.main-scroll` at `thin` with a themed `scrollbar-color`, `tabindex="0"` and an accessible name resolved through `aria-labelledby` to the page heading; `.primary-nav` (`Main`), `.sidebar` (`Workspace navigation`) and `.data-table-scroll` (`Authorized people`) all `thin`, tokenized and focusable; `.action-launcher-dialog` tokenized and named `Go to`, deliberately not focusable itself because focus belongs on its input under the standard ARIA dialog pattern. **UXAUDIT-008's matched pair survived the consolidation**, which was the main regression risk: `.data-table-scroll` still computes `max-height: 738px` together with `overflow-y: auto` in the same context, its `th` still `sticky`, 20 rows rendered -- the pairing whose split clipped 16 workers unreachably earlier the same day, and the rule-level invariant test still guards it. Three RED clauses did not reproduce and were deliberately left alone rather than rebuilt: scroll chaining is already prevented because all regions compute `overscroll-behavior: contain`; `html` and `body` both compute `overflow: hidden`, so popovers cannot create accidental body scroll; and sticky headers do not detach, proven in UXAUDIT-008 by 0px column drift across all six columns scrolled fully right and 200px down. `.main-scroll` keeps `overflow-x: hidden` as a deliberate decision -- every region beneath it that can need horizontal scroll owns its own, and a regression test pins `.data-table-scroll` keeping horizontal overflow so wide content cannot be stranded by the shell's hidden axis. All five tests were mutation-verified against a real break and observed failing before restore: removing `scrollbar-width` from the new `.main-scroll` rule failed the PRIMARY naming the missing token; setting `Focusable: false` on `.main-scroll` failed the BROWSER with `page region ... is not keyboard-focusable`; removing the `Aria` map from `.sidebar` failed the ACCESSIBILITY with `element has no accessible name`; rendering a duplicate region with the same id failed the PERFORMANCE with `id="data-table-scroll" occurrences = 2, want exactly 1`; and reintroducing UXAUDIT-008's exact broken pairing failed the REGRESSION with the same message its own historical comment records. **Boundaries, named rather than glossed.** A shared `scroll-region` marker class was deliberately not added to the DOM -- a first attempt broke roughly eight pre-existing tests that assert exact `class=` values -- so the five regions are reached through one comma-joined selector list built from an exported `ScrollRegionSelectors` list instead, keeping the single source of truth in Go without changing rendered markup. Scroll-edge shadows are scoped only to `.data-table-scroll`, which is already `position: relative`; adding `position: relative` blind to the other four risked changing the containing block for an unaudited absolutely-positioned descendant. The shell itself owns no `ScrollRegion` because its contract is to declare no scroll of its own and defer to the five, which an existing test already pins. `scroll_restoration_wasm_test.go` compiles under `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` but this repository's CI never executes wasm tests, so only its compilation is proven. Two golden shell digests were re-pinned for the new `tabindex`/`id` attributes after diffing the rendered markup and confirming only the intended attributes changed.

## 73. Workflow engine plan-vs-implementation gaps (2026-09-14)

A read-only review of [the workflow runtime spec](specs/workflow-runtime.md) against the served implementation found the kernel libraries largely built but a narrow, partly stubbed production path. These todos cover gaps no existing todo tracks; ticked todos the code did not satisfy were reopened in place with a dated note. A checkbox requires the named tests and proof on the composed serve path, not a library-only harness.

- [ ] `WF-RUN-034` **[GATE_B][SOL_HIGH] Execute real promotion steps through the capability gateway on the served path.**
  - **Depends:** `WF-RUN-002`, `CAP-002`, `EP-PROMO-001`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.REWARDS,BI.WORKFORCE; DIRECT=none; WHY=make served EXECUTE perform and govern the promotion's decisions and effects instead of fabricating outcomes`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_WF_RUN_034`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_WF_RUN_034`; `INTEGRATION=TestTodo_WF_RUN_034_Integration`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_WF_RUN_034_Security`; `FAULT=TestTodo_WF_RUN_034_Fault`; `MUTATION=TestTodo_WF_RUN_034_Mutation`.
  - **RED:** served EXECUTE returns SUCCEEDED/VALID/PASS for CAPABILITY, DECISION and OBSERVE nodes without evaluating them (`runExecuteStep` in `internal/platform/execution/execution.go`), and no EXECUTE node passes the capability gateway.
  - **GREEN:** the composed serve path runs `promotionsteps` for every node, each capability invocation passes the gateway with principal, purpose, deadline, idempotency key and declared effect set, a denied or failed decision routes its real outcome, and no fabricated outcome remains reachable.
  - **REFACTOR:** delete the stub runner; one step-runner composition serves execute and simulate modes.
  - **Refs:** [capability invocation contract](specs/workflow-runtime.md), `internal/platform/execution`, `internal/platform/execution/promotionsteps`, `internal/capability`.

  - **Depends:** `WF-COMP-006`, `EP-WF-002`, `OBS-024`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.ALL; DIRECT=none; WHY=keep publication, quarantine, evidence and intervention audit truthful across restart`.

  - **REFACTOR:** in-memory stores remain test doubles only; a composition test fails if serve wires one.

  - **Depends:** `WF-RUN-002`, `WF-RUN-004`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.ALL; DIRECT=none; WHY=prevent a superseded replica from committing or emitting effects`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_WF_RUN_036`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_WF_RUN_036`; `RACE=TestTodo_WF_RUN_036_Race`; `FAULT=TestTodo_WF_RUN_036_Fault`; `MUTATION=TestTodo_WF_RUN_036_Mutation`.

  - **REFACTOR:** obligations reuse the operator gateway journal.

- [ ] `WF-RUN-040` **[GATE_B][SOL_HIGH] Enforce execution mode per node at runtime and carry a typed execution context.**
  - **Depends:** `WF-COMP-003`, `WF-RUN-002`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.ALL; DIRECT=none; WHY=stop a node from running in a mode it was not compiled for and give steps the locale, legal and entitlement context they need`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_WF_RUN_040`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_WF_RUN_040`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_WF_RUN_040_Security`; `MUTATION=TestTodo_WF_RUN_040_Mutation`.
  - **RED:** the driver never checks instance mode against a node's allowed modes, ExecuteIntent hardcodes EXECUTE, and no WorkflowExecutionContext (locale, legal, entitlement, risk, runtime version) reaches steps.
  - **GREEN:** the driver refuses a node outside its compiled modes before any effect, and every step receives an immutable typed execution context pinned at start.
  - **REFACTOR:** simulate, replay and shadow share the same mode gate.
  - **Refs:** [execution modes](specs/workflow-runtime.md), [execution context](specs/workflow-runtime.md).

- [ ] `WF-STEP-018` **[GATE_B][SOL_HIGH] Complete multi-approver quorum, invalidation and atomic decision-advance.**
  - **Depends:** `WF-STEP-003`, `APPROVAL-007`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.ALL; DIRECT=none; WHY=support real approval policies and never advance on a stale or partial decision`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_WF_STEP_018`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_WF_STEP_018`; `RACE=TestTodo_WF_STEP_018_Race`; `SECURITY=TestTodo_WF_STEP_018_Security`; `FAULT=TestTodo_WF_STEP_018_Fault`.
  - **RED:** quorum greater than one cannot complete, requirement invalidators never fire, and the approval decision and workflow advance commit in separate transactions.
  - **GREEN:** quorum and distinct-approver rules complete correctly, material changes fire invalidators that withdraw pending decisions, and decision plus advance commit atomically or not at all.
  - **REFACTOR:** the promotion journey uses the generic approval kernel rather than a promotion-specific path.
  - **Refs:** [approval and human work kernel](specs/workflow-runtime.md), `internal/workflow/steps/approval`, `internal/humanwork`.

- [ ] `WF-COMP-007` **[GATE_B][SOL_HIGH] Complete the definition type system references.**
  - **Depends:** `WF-COMP-001`, `RULE-001`.
  - **INTENT CONTEXT:** `ROLE=DOMAIN_SUPPORT; SETS=BI.ALL; DIRECT=none; WHY=let definitions declare resolvers, timeouts and compensation that the compiler can check`.
  - **TEST:** `TestTodo_WF_COMP_007`.
  - **TEST MATRIX:** `PRIMARY=TestTodo_WF_COMP_007`; `PROPERTY=TestTodo_WF_COMP_007_Property`; `MUTATION=TestTodo_WF_COMP_007_Mutation`.
  - **RED:** definitions cannot declare resolver_ref, timeout_policy or compensation_ref, rule_ref is an unresolved string, schema refs are only syntax-checked, and there is no WorkflowVariableRevision record.
  - **GREEN:** the compiler resolves every reference against published registries, rejects unknown or retired targets, and variable writes append revisions.
  - **REFACTOR:** reference resolution is one pass shared by all step types.
  - **Refs:** [declarative definition and type system](specs/workflow-runtime.md), `internal/workflow`.
